To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concept of ESD should be based on the preservation of all the crucial natural capital, including all the natural resources, and that the crucial natural capital should be identified by a set of operational criteria and principles.

(1) ESD is a concept with many different definitions; (2) ESD is not a concept that is widely accepted by the coastal experts; and (3) ESD should be based on an integrated approach, which is a combination of strong and weak ESD approaches.

the approaches to ESD which include the operational criteria of natural sciences and which are consistent with the principles of weak sustainability are considered as most functional as well as the most scientifically appropriate to define the target of E SD in coastal ecosystems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new paradigm of sustainable development, based on the concept of Ecologically Sustainable Economic Welfare, that is a more operational and scientific approach to the concept of ESD.
the development of a conceptual model that integrates natural sciences with social sciences in the context of sustainable development.
the development of an integrated approach to ESD that is based on a holistic and multidisciplinary understanding of the complex relationships between the natural and social systems in coastal areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach of conservation of the critical capital is most functional and appropriate for defining the ESD target in the coastal zone.

the approach to ESD that is based on the preservation of the biological critical level is the best one, but the preservation of the critical natural level and the non-declining welfare per capita approaches are the most functional.
a strong sustainability approach to ESD, based on preservation of all natural capital, is most appropriate for the management of coastal ecosystems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concept of ESD is not only scientifically and practically useful but also that it is an important tool for the sustainable development of coastal ecosystems.
the approaches to ESD should be evaluated in a scientific and interdisciplinary context, and that the evaluation should be performed by the scientific community of the relevant disciplines.
the concept of ESD is a powerful instrument for promoting a sustainable development of coastal areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of natural and social sciences is necessary in order to achieve a sustainable development in coastal ecosystems, which is the main objective of this paper.
the integration of natural and social science principles in a single framework is a necessary step for achieving a more comprehensive understanding of coastal sustainability.

the ESD target should be defined in terms of the preservation of the critical natural assets and the crucial ecosystem services, while the economic and social dimensions should be considered within a framework that allows for the identification of a set of sustainable options.
